course_description:
This course introduces foundation economic concepts as they apply to the broader tourism sector which includes the hospitality and event industries. Adopting a macro perspective, the course examines demand and supply, market structures, the influence of economic change on the sector, and the role of the tourism, hospitality and event industries in the economy. Economic concepts that apply to the tourism sector are explored including economic impact assessment and environmental economics.

This course is a foundation for your future career in the private or public sector, where an understanding of economics is essential for effective tourism business or policy management. The course will develop your capability in using selected economic concepts and analysis approaches, applied to tourism. The first part of the course delivers fundamental principles and concepts, such asﾠthe forces of demand and supply, market structures and the issues of externalities and public goods. The second part of the course deals with theﾠinfluence of economic change on tourism and the role of tourism in the economy. This section covers some useful concepts and tools, including economic contributions of tourism, cost benefit analysis and environmental economics. Various examples will be used to demonstrate how economic concepts and principles are applied to tourism.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

Previous student feedback indicated that students appreciated the clear course structure, weekly test banks, tutorial activities, and personalised feedback, while also expressing a desire for more interactive learning opportunities, clearer assessment guidance, and stronger connections between economic concepts and real-world tourism practice. In response, this course has been enhanced with additional applied tutorial activities, authentic case studies, and scaffolded assessment support to promote active engagement and practical application of course concepts.

To meet The University of Queensland's requirements for secure assessment, Assessment 3 now includes an Interactive Oral Assessment (IOA). Following the submission of the recorded team presentation, each student will participate in a live question-and-answer session with their tutor. This provides students with an opportunity to demonstrate their individual understanding of the course content, explain and justify their team's analysis and recommendations, and verify their engagement with the group assessment while maintaining academic integrity.

assessment_details.task_description: The test-bank exercises, consisting of 7 chapters, are designed to assist students with self-practice and self-learning. Students can choose which chapters they want to complete and submit. Multiple attempts per chapter are allowed. Students will be awarded two (2) points upon completing one chapter (provided more than 80% of the questions have been answered correctly). A maximum of 10 points for this assessment in the final grade is awarded if students complete at least five (5) chapters throughout the semester. A test bank, consisting of practical questions that integrate economic concepts and tourism issues, is adopted to assist students with self-practice and self-learning. It includes (1) basic questions that allow students to better comprehend the theory and concepts, and (2) advanced applied questions that discuss the impacts of COVID-19, sustainability, and global mega trends on tourism, businesses, and policies. Students need to engage with the test bank weekly, starting from week 3 to week 10. Each weekly test bank, consisting of 10 multiple-choice questions and two to three open-ended questions, is designed to align with the lecture taught that week. This allows students to review the concepts and test their knowledge by working with the questions. Correct answers will be provided once students submit their responses. learning_activities.topic: Introduction to economics and tourism This week, we will introduce the fundamentals of tourism economics, explain key economic concepts, explore the tourism system, and examine how economics informs consumer, business, and government decision-making.

Demand concepts I (The law demand and elasticity of demand) Our lecture will explain the law of demand, factors influencing tourism demand, movements and shifts in the demand curve, and the application of elasticity concepts to tourism, hospitality, and event markets.

Introduction to assessments This week's tutorial will provide an overview of the course assessments and expectations, help you connect with your classmates, clarify assessment requirements, and establish groups for the semester's presentation project.

Demand Concepts II (Total revenue & Demand modelling and forecasting) This week, our lecture will explain the relationship between price elasticity and total revenue, and introduce tourism demand modelling and forecasting to support pricing, marketing, and investment decisions in tourism, hospitality, and events.

Demand curve and elasticity This week's tutorial will reinforce demand concepts through collaborative exercises and Assessment 1: Test Bank 1, applying the law of demand, elasticity, total revenue, and tourism demand forecasting to analyse real-world tourism scenarios Ekka Public Holiday - Wednesday 12th August 2026 - Check Blackboard for announcements about affected classes.

Supply concepts I (Law of supply, Elasticity of supply & Production and costs) This week, our lecture will explain the law of supply, factors influencing tourism supply, price elasticity of supply, and the role of production, costs, and factors of production in tourism, hospitality, and event businesses.

Marginal revenue & Demand forecasting This week's tutorial wil l reinforce demand and supply concepts through Assessment 1: Test Bank 2, applying total revenue, elasticity, and tourism demand forecasting to real-world tourism and airline pricing scenarios.

Supply concepts II (Long run costs & Returns to scale) This week, our lecture will explain short-run and long-run production costs, profit maximisation, and the role of economies and diseconomies of scale in shaping business expansion decisions in tourism, hospitality, and events.

Supply concepts I This week's tutorial will reinforce supply concepts through Assessment 1: Test Bank 3, applying production costs, supply decisions, and economies of scale to real-world tourism and hospitality case studies.

Market equilibrium This week, our lecture will explain how market equilibrium is determined through the interaction of demand and supply, and examine how macroeconomic indicators—including GDP, commodity prices, interest rates, and exchange rates—influence tourism demand, supply, and market outcomes.

Supply concepts II This week's tutorial explores tourism supply and cost concepts by applying cost analysis, economies of scale, diminishing marginal returns, and marginal decision-making principles to determine the profit-maximising output of tourism and hospitality businesses, while supporting preparation for Assessment 1 through Test Bank 4.

Market structure and strategies This week's lecture examines tourism market structures and competitive strategies by analysing pricing, product differentiation, cost leadership, strategic alliances, and business growth strategies.

Market equilibrium This week's tutorial applies market equilibrium concepts and evaluates how changes in GDP, interest rates, exchange rates, and commodity prices influence tourism markets, while preparing students for Assessment 1 through Test Bank 5.

Economic impact of tourism This week's lecture explores the economic contribution of tourism by analysing Tourism Satellite Accounts (TSA), interpreting key tourism economic indicators, and evaluating tourism's contribution to GDP, employment, exports, and regional development.

Market structure and pricing This week's tutorial applies market structure concepts and competitive strategies through case studies and problem-solving activities on product differentiation, cost leadership, vertical integration, and pricing strategies, while supporting preparation for Assessment 1 through Test Bank 6.

Teamwork dynamics + Exam review The Employability Team will deliver a guest lecture and interactive workshop on teamwork dynamics to strengthen students' collaboration, communication, and conflict management skills for group projects. This will be followed by an Assessment 2 exam review and consultation session. As important assessment and employability skills will be covered, all students are strongly encouraged to attend.

Economic impact of tourism This week's tutorial develops students' ability to interpret Tourism Satellite Account (TSA) data by analysing tourism's direct economic contribution at the national and regional levels, while supporting preparation for Assessment 1 through Test Bank 7.
In-semester break

In-class exam Assessment 2 (In-class Exam) will be held during the scheduled lecture time in the usual lecture venue. Please refer to Blackboard (Assessment 2) for detailed information regarding the exam format, permitted materials, and other assessment requirements.

Assignment 3 discussion and consultation This week's tutorial includes an overview of Assessment 3, with opportunities for discussion, feedback, and consultation to support students in planning and developing their assignment King’s Birthday Public Holiday - Monday 5th October 2026 - Check Blackboard for announcements about affected classes.

Economic assessment of events This week's lecture applies economic evaluation methods for events by analysing direct in-scope expenditure, return on investment, economic impact assessment, and cost–benefit analysis to evaluate the economic value of tourism and special events.

Review the in-class exam This week's tutorial reviews the Assessment 2 in-class exam responses to reinforce key economic concepts, followed by group consultation and feedback to support the development of Assessment 3.

Tourism, environment and climate change This week's lecture applies economic evaluation methods to assess the costs and benefits of tourism and special events through case studies, while examining market failure, environmental externalities, and the tourism carbon footprint to support sustainable decision-making.

Economic assessment of events This week's tutorial applies economic evaluation techniques to analyse the costs and benefits of special events through real-world case studies, with a focus on Direct In-scope Expenditure (DISE), Return on Investment (ROI), Economic Impact Assessment (EIA), and Cost–Benefit Analysis (CBA).

Course review & summary This final lecture explores strategies for mitigating tourism-related carbon emissions through the roles of governments, businesses, and tourists. The session concludes by reviewing the key economic concepts and learning outcomes developed throughout the course, highlighting how students have applied these principles in their Assessment 3 presentations to address contemporary tourism challenges.

Assignment 3 (Part B - Team Q&A/Interactive oral assessment) Assessment 3 comprises two components. Part A is a recorded team presentation, which must be submitted in Week 12. Part B is an interactive oral assessment (Team Q&A) conducted as a live question-and-answer session with your tutor during the Week 13 tutorial. During the oral assessment, each student will individually respond to a series of randomly selected questions related to their team's recorded presentation (Part A). The purpose of the oral assessment is to verify each student's understanding of the team's analysis, assess their ability to apply economic concepts and justify their recommendations, and ensure individual engagement with the group task.
